preamble: Reduction of the alveolar trill [r] to a single-contact tap [ɾ] turns several rapid tongue-tip contacts into one. It happened historically in Greek, where Ancient Greek ρ, described as a trill, is prototypically a tap in the modern language. It also occurs synchronically in Italian, where single intervocalic /r/ is often a one-contact trill, effectively a tap, especially in unstressed syllables.

examples.from: Ancient Greek ῥῆμα with ρ = trill [r] (initially voiceless [r̥])
examples.note: Ancient rho was an alveolar trill; the only Modern Greek rhotic is prototypically an alveolar tap, with a trill surviving mainly in clusters.
Single intervocalic /r/ is realized with one or two contacts and often treated as a tap, especially in unstressed syllables, whereas geminate /rr/ keeps three to seven contacts.
